parts:
Hi,

Have you tried your code for a single region?

i is an integer value, data1$region is a factor I'd make
data1$region character:
data1$region <- as.character(data1$region)
and loop over: for( i in unique(data1$region) ){
(although I'd probably do it with lapply rather than a for-loop and create
a list of plots for future printing)

> dt1 = data1[data1$region==i, ]

Your data subset is in dt1 and then you plot dt
> p <- ggplot(dt, aes(x = class, y = value)) +

"identity", and further down "bold" have curly double quotes. My R
wouldn¹t accept this when I cut and pasted it.

> geom_bar(stat = ³identity" ) +
> theme_bw()+
> theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size=8, color="black"),
> axis.text.y = element_text(size=8, color="black"),
> legend.text=element_text(size=10 ),
> plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = ³bold", colour =
>"black", vjust = -1 ))+
> coord_flip()+
> facet_wrap(~ year)

If you have the plots working, you will be over-writing the plot on the
screen, unless you have opened a multipage device, but you didn't specify
this in your code.

> print(p)
>}

Ron.

yes, it works great when I manually filter for each single region, but since I have a large dataset with 100+ regions it would make more sense to me to speed things up a bit, hence this idea to save each region on a different page

 
here is the single region code (no curly quotes):

 library(dplyr)

 ggplot(data1, aes(x = age_num, y = value, col=year)) +
 geom_bar( filter( data1, region=="region13") , stat = "identity") +
 theme_bw()+
 coord_flip()+
 facet_wrap(~year)

I see this, and do it myself. My question was because the code you sent
didn't work if, for example, I set i<-1 and then ran the code within the
loop, for various reasons including the integer to character/factor
comparison and plotting one data.frame having created a different one.

>here is the single region code:
>
>library(dplyr)
>
>ggplot(data1, aes(x = age_num, y = value, col=year)) +

> geom_bar( filter( data1, region==³region13²) , stat = ³identity²) +
> theme_bw()+
> coord_flip()+
> facet_wrap(~year)


Something like this works for me:

# plot
pp<-lapply( levels(data1$region), function(rr){
ggplot(data1[data1$region==rr,])+
geom_bar(aes(x=class,y=value),
stat="identity")+
theme_bw()+
coord_flip()+
facet_wrap(~year)+
labs(title=rr) } )
# print to multiple pages
pdf('ale.pdf')
invisible(lapply(pp,print))
dev.off()



Ron.
